claim: Owned local broker and message engine installation, native service recovery, scoped semantic retrieval, and Codex registry promotion passed within their stated scopes; managed Codex automatic push remains held after an observed unsubmitted message.
limitations: This is local integration evidence. It does not establish complete foundation acceptance, a quality winner, physical-host reboot recovery or paper-broker acceptance.

Managed Codex PTY submission failed despite native read metadata. Neither reader status nor the successful initial peer exchange establishes ordinary automatic submission, busy delivery or offline catch-up.
The Relay native adapter was not substituted: it bundles an older Codex and disables web search by default; selected-client parity is unverified.
The unchanged Relay default test suite retains one failed lifecycle timeout. Its focused longer-timeout pass does not make that default suite green.

Hindsight capture is enabled only in the three explicitly mapped owned folders. The original checkout retains its incumbent memory writer. Cold git seeding and remaining knowledge pages have separate results.
RAG observations establish indexing and one retrieval, not retrieval-quality or financial-research acceptance. Client, backend and cache counters are not combined; monetary cost is unknown.

installation_and_lifecycle.scope: New owned runtime, credential home, local namespace, database volume and user units; provider HOME and existing native sign-ins preserved.
installation_and_lifecycle.independent_release_observation: Native agent list empty; both owned client and worker processes absent.
installation_and_lifecycle.engine_version_observation: Native npm listing reports @relaycast/engine 8.14.0. Its health endpoint reports hardcoded 0.1.0 and is not used as package identity.

hindsight_ensure.boot_and_unhealthy_recovery: source-supported; no physical-host reboot or forced crash executed

installation_and_lifecycle.relay_unit: Foreground native node up --no-spawn with scoped working directory, native dotenv, existing ecosystem PATH and Restart=on-failure; no wrapper or custom bridge.
initial_failed_conditions: Upstream deployment container build succeeded, but runtime rejected loopback HTTP with exit 64. It was stopped and replaced by the documented native engine composed with an ordinary pinned Node container.
A copied Node image digest initially failed resolution; the exact digest was corrected from the upstream Dockerfile.
Broker background startup hit the upstream unbounded TCP preflight. Supported port-zero atomic bind resolved that startup path.
An alternate state directory was incompatible with spawn/list state discovery. Qualification moved to the owned project's canonical state.
A broker identity owned by the earlier state returned HTTP 409; a distinct supported broker name started successfully.
